text: Mr Louis Ng conveyed feedback that the initial surge of male Aedes mosquitoes released under Project Wolbachia causes discomfort to residents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I hope to reassure residents that these male mosquitoes do not bite or transmit diseases – I say this in Parliament – and ask residents to be patient and bear with the initial surge.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are considering the expansion of Project Wolbachia to more neighbourhoods, in consultation with NEA's Dengue Expert Advisory Panel.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is a new and important means to future-proof ourselves against the faster breeding of mosquitoes, as a result of higher temperatures brought by climate change.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Just as NEA is establishing mosquito farms, Singapore Food Agency (SFA) is transforming food farms.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Food, like water, is a resource that can be disrupted by climate change.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In Asia alone, we expect an additional 250 million mouths to feed by 2030.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Yet, the amount of arable land could fall by 5% due to climate change and environmental degradation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Singapore, which currently imports more than 90% of our food, will be vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the face of these changes, we have developed three food baskets to ensure our food security by diversifying food sources, growing food overseas and growing local.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have designated 2020 as the Year of Singapore Food story to focus our national effort and attention.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about the Government's success in food source diversification and its role in mitigating price hikes during supply disruptions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This did not come by chance, but is a result of SFA's continuous efforts.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While the Government does our part, we require the industry to also be pro-active in diversifying supply sources to enhance business resiliency.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, since last year, SFA has introduced requirements for egg importers to adopt plans to mitigate the impact of any supply disruptions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: With a well-diversified food supply, Singapore can reduce the impact of food supply shortages and price changes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, consumers need to be mindful that the price of any particular food item is determined by a combination of factors, including import prices, exchange rates and profit margins which suppliers can command.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui and Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about how the Government is helping the local agri-food industry grow.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As a small country with limited space, our land use faces many competing needs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have dedicated less than 1% of our land for agriculture today.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Within such tight land constraints, the "30 by 30" vision is highly ambitious, especially if we must achieve it within the same 1%.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Yet, having visited some of our new-tech farms, I am optimistic that it is achievable if we invest in an innovative agri-food sector.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Since 2017, SFA has been awarding agriculture land, through a competitive land tender basis, to agri-food companies with promising technologies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: One such company is Green Harvest, a local vegetable farm.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The farm uses modern greenhouse growing techniques which mitigates the impact of unfavourable weather conditions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This study will consider feedback from farmers for centralised facilities and services to reduce the cost of food production.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The study will also introduce circular economy principles, so that the by-product of one farm can be used as an input for another.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SFA will work with farms, including successful tenders in recent land sales exercises, to work towards an exciting vision for Lim Chu Kang.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SFA's plans for Lim Chu Kang will complement the development of the Agri-Food Innovation Park (AFIP), which we announced last year as a high-tech agri-food cluster in Sungei Kadut.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The food production innovations developed in AFIP can scale up in Lim Chu Kang to contribute towards our "30 by 30" vision.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SFA will also look to unlock the potential of farming at sea.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Last week, I accompanied President Halimah to visit Eco-Ark.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Eco-Ark's CEO Mr Leow Ban Tat, who had decades of experience in marine and off-shore engineering, including in Keppel, applied principles of oil rigs construction to that of a floating fish farm.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: He worked with his team to conceptualise, design and integrate a floating platform with closed-containment aquaculture technologies that treat influent sea water used to cultivate fish.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These technologies mitigate the effects of pollution and algae blooms that threaten both farms and our marine environment.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ideas like this is how we will transform fish farming practices so that they are more productive, sustainable and climate-resilient.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will ensure that such aquaculture is productive and environmentally responsible, such as shown by Barramundi Asia, Singapore's first and only deep-sea fish farm.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SFA will work with stakeholders to study this.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are supporting different modes of fish farming.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Where water quality is good, farms can carry out deep sea farming.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Where it is not, farms can adopt closed-containment technologies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Where there can be synergies with land-based water and waste systems, land-based aquaculture can be conducted.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Like land, every space at sea can be used for food production but must be judiciously managed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh also asked how the Government is helping local farms remain competitive.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Over the years, our economic agencies have been supporting local farms in their overseas expansion.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Growing their businesses overseas allow farms to tap on land and manpower, lower production costs, and break into new markets.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I encourage our farms to take a leaf from the food manufacturing industry, where companies like Tee Yih Jia Food anchor their expertise locally while expanding operations overseas.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Some of our farms, like Apollo, have already done so.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These food products produced overseas, while not "Made in Singapore", should be marketed as "Made by Singapore", since they uphold the same reputation for high quality and standards as those produced domestically.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To complement these efforts, SFA, Enterprise Singapore and the industry will be developing Clean-Green Standards for urban farms which harness resource-efficient technologies to produce food in cleaner environments.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They will study ways to incorporate information that more people are concerned about, such as the carbon footprint of food they produce.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The standards will serve as a mark of quality assurance that our farms can use to differentiate their products in the market.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Beyond this, we will review how we can expand our support for technology test-bedding, adoption and resource efficiency in our farms.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: New innovations to produce food more productively and sustainably are also needed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: One theme under this research programme is the production of novel foods, like alternative proteins.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Traditional meat production methods are often land and water intensive, and generate high levels of emissions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Today, alternative proteins, such as Impossible and Quorn, are poised to become game-changers.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I hope Members will enjoy the alternative protein food items from Tee Yih Jia Food and Empress served at today's tea break after our speeches.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui asked about food safety of novel foods.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will ensure that only novel foods that are safe for consumption are introduced in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This framework facilitates the sale of alternative proteins in Singapore while ensuring their safety.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Companies, such as local start-up Shiok Meats, who is looking to produce cell-cultured shrimp, will be able to benefit from this framework.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To support the assessment of novel food, SFA will establish an international expert working group to provide scientific advice on food safety.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Beyond food supply, we must not also forget our fundamental mission, that is to ensure that the food we eat is safe.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SFA takes a serious approach towards upholding high food safety and hygiene standards.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Since its formation, SFA has conducted more than 5,200 inspections in 2019 and taken more than 1,600 enforcement actions against errant operators.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SFA will be introducing new measures to safeguard food safety.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Premises which pose higher food safety risks, such as caterers and central kitchens, will be required to install closed-circuit television cameras.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This enables them to monitor food safety performance and provide evidence in the event of food safety allegations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Enhanced measures will also be targeted at businesses that cater to vulnerable groups.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Food businesses catering to preschools, kindergartens and nursing homes will be required to maintain food retention samples, which will facilitate investigations during food-borne outbreaks.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This way, SFA can re-prioritise resources to focus on checks to ensure compliance with food safety requirements.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the introduction of a Good Samaritan Food Donation Act.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Any legislation will need to strike a balance between facilitating food donation and ensuring food safety.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will be happy to work with Mr Louis Ng.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Chairman, let me conclude my last section of my speech by touching on the role of all Singaporeans in taking climate action.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As the Government, we are providing leadership in tackling climate change.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We do this by enhancing our climate pledge under the Paris Agreement and working with the industry to guide their transformation to a low-carbon economy.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While the Government can lead on sustainability, the people must champion its cause.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For instance, Singaporeans can make conscious climate-friendly choices in our daily essentials, such as food.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Locally-produced food is of high quality, incurs less carbon miles, lasts longer and tastes good.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: By eating local, Singaporeans are making an environmentally sustainable choice.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the process, we support our farmers by choosing food that is grown in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Since 2017, SFA has partnered Singapore Agro-Food Enterprises Federation (SAFEF) to organise farmers' markets to raise awareness of local produce.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Last month, I unveiled a new logo which Singapore farmers can soon use to help Singaporeans identify local produce.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The community can also support local production by participating in community farming projects.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, nearly 80% of NParks' Community in Bloom gardens grow edibles.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There is also potential for companies and the community to engage in commercial urban farming that involves the community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Since the launch of the pilot rooftop farm, Citiponics in Ang Mo Kio, interest from the public – as Er Dr Lee Bee Wah mentioned just now – has increased towards urban farming in community spaces.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will provide more opportunities for urban rooftop farming.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the coming months, SFA will tender 16 rooftop spaces on HDB multi-storey car parks across the island, totalling over 30,000 sqm.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As we grow our agri-sector, let us get involved in growing food in our own backyards.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They are amongst the top three highest energy-consuming household appliances today.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, many households continue to purchase 1 to 2 ticks refrigerators, partly due to the higher upfront costs of energy-efficient models, without considering the savings from electricity consumption over the long term.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Similarly, showering takes up a significant proportion of water consumption, yet many households are choosing the less water-efficient fittings.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These households will receive a once-off $150 voucher to purchase refrigerator models approved by NEA that have 3 ticks and above.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Not only will this help fight climate change, households can benefit from electricity cost savings of up to $60 annually.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will also extend the "Switch and Save – use LED" programme launched in 2018 to all 3-room HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In addition, we will give all 1 to 3-room HDB households a $50 voucher to offset the cost of changing their shower fittings to more water-efficient 3-tick models.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Next, let me focus on the ground-up efforts of our youths and citizens to address climate change.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I commend our youths who are channelling their passions into positive change for the environment.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: During the Year of Climate Action in 2018, more than two climate-related activities per day were conducted, and youths played a big part in them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Recently, a group of 50 youths participated in the Environmental Track of the Youth Action Challenge organised by MCCY, submitting projects ranging from waste reduction to green technologies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We work together with these youths to deliver some of these ideas into reality.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To empower our youths with knowledge and experience on sustainability, my Ministry is working with MOE and the National Youth Council (NYC).

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We want to introduce more sustainability programmes in schools and community facilities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Even Outward Bound Singapore (OBS) @ Coney will be designed to be a eco-experience for our youths to learn and enjoy.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Government will work with schools to introduce initiatives which will integrate green infrastructure, sustainability programmes and curriculum design to inculcate positive environmental values in our youths, like ones done in Mee Toh School.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Another group of Singaporeans whose efforts I would like to recognise are those that are willing to share their experiences and ideas on sustainability.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Last year, my Ministry convened our first Citizens' Workgroup on recycling, where 48 participants joined us on a month-long journey of co-creation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will be setting up two more Citizens' Workgroups this year, focusing on more issues that Singaporeans care about.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: One Workgroup will start the conversation on how we can increase demand for local produce.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I invite interested members of the public to visit our website at foodstory.sg to find out more about the Workgroup and sign up for it.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As we have done with the recycling workgroup, we will carefully consider and work with these workgroups to realise some of their recommendations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is our aspiration for Singapore as a nation to practise sustainable development and put sustainability at the centre of the way we live, work and play.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At Budget, the Deputy Prime Minister spoke about the Ministry of National Development's (MND) Green Towns Programme, which injects sustainability into the infrastructure of HDB towns.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Beyond the look and feel of housing estates, MEWR will introduce initiatives that will encourage Singaporeans to live and breathe sustainability.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: First, as we rejuvenate neighbourhoods, we will create more sustainable community touchpoints.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will build sustainable hawker centres that strive towards zero waste.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Second, we will introduce community-based programmes that foster sustainability initiatives on the ground.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Third, we will develop indicators for towns to track their progress and benchmark against national sustainability targets in carbon, energy, water and recycling.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This will drive home the message that the effort of each and every Singaporean counts.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In Tampines, we are piloting new sustainability projects which can be replicated in other towns.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Residents from 12 HDB blocks will be segregating food waste generated in their homes, to be fed to black soldier fly larvae.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The larvae will produce fertiliser for a new vertical vegetable farm, and the larvae will be fed to tilapia cultivated in the Tampines Park pond.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Not only will this project reduce food waste, it will simultaneously strengthen the community's food resilience.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The second project in a different part of Tampines is the introduction of "Eco Boards".

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Eco Boards are low-energy digital boards that provide block-level information on water and energy use to residents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Together with Singapore Power and Temasek, we plan to build Eco Boards in several sites across Tampines Town.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These Eco Boards will enhance the residents' awareness of their resource usage and illustrate the impact of green infrastructure such as solar panels.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: More details on the three Eco Towns will be announced over the coming months.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I believe that the success of these Eco Towns will inspire other towns to begin their own journey of transformation towards sustainability.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To build our sustainable Singapore together with Singaporeans, Deputy Prime Minister announced at Budget the establishment of a Singapore Eco Fund.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We welcome project proposals which involve the community and can deliver measurable impacts on our sustainability goals.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When we started our journey as a nation, our founding fathers gave us a vision of being the cleanest and greenest city in Southeast Asia.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Even for this, we were inspired to do it together.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew said in 1968 at the launch of the inaugural "Keep Singapore Clean" campaign, "For only a people with high social and educational standards can maintain a clean and green city".

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And he went on to say, "Only a people proud of their community performance, feeling for the well-being of their fellow citizens, can keep up high personal and public standards of hygiene." We are now on our journey towards a sustainable and climate friendly Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is a journey that we can only make together.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Prime Minister, at a tree-planting event in 2014, said, "But we also have to do more than just plant trees; we also have to make the whole of the environment sustainable, friendly to people, and also for Singaporeans to be friendly to the environment".

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is for this reason that the Government will place sustainability at the core of everything we do.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, only by living and practising sustainability together can we mitigate the impacts of climate change and secure the resources needed to take Singapore into the future.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Let us all play our part and work together, as one people, to ensure that Singapore remains a liveable home for our future generations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Chairman, I will now hand over to Senior Minister of State Dr Amy Khor to address other strategies that will make Singapore a clean, sustainable and liveable home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Chairman, as Minister Masagos said earlier, we each have a duty to take climate action and safeguard Singapore for our future generations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This was why we designated 2019 as Singapore's Year Towards Zero Waste – to mobilise every Singaporean to do their part towards a Zero Waste nation and a circular economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We supported ground-up initiatives through the "Towards Zero Waste Grant" and launched the "Say YES to Waste Less" campaign.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: All these efforts helped to instil in Singaporeans the 3Rs of Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We can close our resource loops, just as we have done for our Water Story.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In fact, we already recycle 99% of	our	ferrous	metal	waste and	construction	and demolition waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As shared in Budget 2020, we are also making good progress turning incineration ash into construction material we proudly call NEWSand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will begin trials to test potential NEWSand materials in road construction along Tanah Merah Coast Road later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Achieving our Zero Waste vision is a whole-of-nation effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Last year, we convened our first ever Citizens' Workgroup to co-create solutions to #RecycleRight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: One follow-up project is the redesigning of the blue recycling bin to be more user-friendly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Their ideas include a transparent panel on the bin body, eye-level labels with #RecycleRight information and tailored deposit holes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MEWR and NEA will support the Workgroup members to fine-tune and trial their prototype.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ms Joan Pereira may also be pleased to know that NEA has already successfully trialled the use of bigger recycling bins, which are collected by side-loader trucks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These	will	be	progressively	deployed across Singapore by end-2022.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As Mr Daniel Goh highlighted, grassroots efforts are also	important	in	encouraging	households	to #RecycleRight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our Public Waste Collectors work with the grassroots to organise Cash-for-Trash programmes regularly at convenient locations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: NEA is also considering a pilot "recycling bin contamination rate" competition involving several Residents' Networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The private sector has also come on board.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: F&N Foods partnered NEA in the "Recycle N Save" pilot.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I am encouraged by the positive response with over two million containers collected since the launch last October.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Dennis Tan and Mr Louis Ng spoke about reducing disposables through a ban or a charge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We believe that we should take a pragmatic approach and find an inclusive solution that works for Singapore and Singaporeans, taking into account our local context.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, degradable bags provide little benefits in Singapore as we incinerate all our household waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: On a life cycle basis, single-use paper and degradable bags also consume large amount of resources like water and land.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hence, instead of pursuing a substitution strategy, we should focus on inculcating the right values.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Singaporeans' actions could then be motivated by a consciousness to safeguard the environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is why, in the spirit of Singapore Together, NEA will convene a Citizens' Workgroup later this year to address the excessive consumption of all disposables, including Styrofoam and single-use bags.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We welcome citizens to deliberate the idea of a nation-wide charge for	single-use bags as well as other measures, such as campaigns and education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will take the Workgroup's recommendations seriously and work with participants to implement them where feasible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I invite Singaporeans to register for the Workgroup later this month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Among the supermarkets, FairPrice has taken the lead with their plastic bag charge trial last year, complemented with educational efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The trial has shown promising results, with majority of FairPrice's customers receptive towards a plastic bag charge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I commend FairPrice for its leadership and welcome this decision to expand the trial to 25 outlets for one year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I am	heartened that Prime has also implemented a plastic bag charge in four of their outlets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I call on other supermarkets and retailers to also pilot this and urge Singaporeans to support these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: My Ministry is taking the lead to introduce enabling regulations to transit to a circular economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Last September, we passed the Resource Sustainability Act to address three priority waste streams – packaging waste, e-waste, and food waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Packaging waste makes up a third of the total domestic waste disposed of in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The amount disposed of will only grow as Singaporeans embrace new trends in online shopping and food delivery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We need to find ways to manage packaging waste more sustainably.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This will make companies more aware of their packaging use and encourage them to optimise it, thereby minimising waste and also reducing business costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As this is the first time we are implementing such a reporting requirement, NEA is partnering the Singapore Manufacturing Federation on a	joint capability development programme that will support companies in fulfilling their new obligations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Companies will be offered workshops and training courses to familiarise themselves with the reporting framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Companies can also exchange best practices in sustainable packaging waste management and prepare themselves for the upcoming Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Under the EPR framework, producers are responsible for collecting and recycling their product packaging.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are bringing forward the EPR for packaging waste by implementing it in phases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In a typical DRS, producers pay for the system to take back used beverage containers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Consumers get a refund when returning empty beverage containers at designated return points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The DRS is also an idea proposed by the Citizens' Workgroup on #RecycleRight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Workgroup members will partner NEA to work through the DRS implementation, such as co-designing surveys to optimise outcomes of the DRS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Together with our industry stakeholders and Singaporeans, we will design a DRS suitable for Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: PET bottles and the like can then be processed locally into plastic pellets, which can in turn be	used to make new products.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But not all plastic waste is suitable for mechanical recycling, for example, contaminated plastic bags.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To treat these, we are also pursuing chemical recycling solutions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Chemical recycling can potentially convert these plastics into higher-value products, like pyrolysis oil, which is a potential feedstock for Singapore's petrochemical sector.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If successful, this will move us closer to both our goals of being a Zero Waste nation and a Low-Carbon economy.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu and Mr Mohamed Irshad asked about our progress to address e-waste, which is our second priority waste stream.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Producers have also recently begun collecting data on the	amount of regulated electrical and electronic products supplied in Singapore, for submission to NEA early next year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA is now pre-qualifying organisations for the tender, and aims to appoint the PRS operator by the second half of this year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This will give the operator sufficient lead time to establish its collection and treatment network and organise public outreach programmes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Similar to packaging waste, the e-waste EPR framework will finance and drive local e-waste recycling capabilities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: TES-B, a new lithium-ion battery recycling facility will be completed in the coming months.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: EWR2 and SMC Industrial are also planning to build two recycling facilities dedicated to large household appliances, ICT equipment and batteries.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They will be completed by mid-2020 and mid-2022 respectively.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With these additions, Singapore will be ready to treat our e-waste collected under the EPR system.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Mohamed Irshad spoke about food waste, another major waste stream with high generation tonnage and low recycling rates.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Last year, I announced that from 2024, owners and occupiers of commercial and industrial premises that generate large amounts of food waste will be required to segregate their food waste for treatment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Owners and occupiers of new buildings will also be required to treat their food waste on-site.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These requirements will apply to shopping malls and hotels with more than 3,000 sqm of F&B area, including function area for hotels; as well as industrial premises that either house at least one food manufacturer of more than 750 sqm, or are above 20,000 sqm and have more than 20 food tenants.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA is including these thresholds in the Code of Practice on Environmental Health, to ensure that from 2021 onwards, obligated owners and operators will allocate space for on-site food waste treatment systems in their development plans.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To support premises to prepare for the mandatory requirements, NEA is developing a guidebook on best practices and case studies on the implementation of food waste segregation and treatment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Segregating food waste from the other waste streams will make it easier to maintain cleanliness in premises.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Cleanliness and hygiene is a first line of defence against evolving public health threats.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Seventeen years ago, when we were battling SARS, we instituted regular "spring cleaning" of our hawker centres to safeguard environmental hygiene and curb the spread of such diseases.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Last month, in response to COVID-19, we launched the SG Clean campaign to rally Singaporeans to keep Singapore clean and to safeguard public health.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: At	the individual level, we call on Singaporeans to practise good personal hygiene and social responsibility through the "7 Habits of Good Public Hygiene".

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Concurrently, NEA is working with Government agencies and business premises to step up public hygiene standards.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We want our hawker centres, public transport nodes, schools, retail malls, shops and various premises to receive the "SG Clean" quality mark.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: SG Clean seeks to turn the current crisis into an opportunity, by uplifting the standards of public hygiene and sustaining them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is to be a whole-of-nation movement to instill a national "keep clean culture" for the long term, beyond the battle with COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will need to shift from the current top-down compliance-focused approach towards a more collective approach, where all stakeholders take accountability and ownership to proactively achieve high standards of cleanliness in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The SG Clean effort is needed even if our regular surveys indicate that we are mostly doing well in keeping Singapore clean.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In the last two years, we witnessed multiple incidents of gastroenteritis linked to contaminated environments, including at pre-schools and nursing homes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These incidents underscore the importance of environmental hygiene.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So last August, even before COVID-19, NEA convened an interdisciplinary technical committee to develop a set of national baseline cleaning standards for premises.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA is currently consulting with stakeholders to further develop sector-specific standards.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These standards will comprise a regime for proactive and thorough cleaning, as well as disinfection, at prescribed frequencies.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This will include the oft-neglected "back of house" areas such as bin centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As part of the EPHA amendment, we will place greater accountability on premises managers for the cleanliness of their premises.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They will be required to appoint a Designated Person to assist them to develop an environmental sanitation programme and advise on measures to remedy any lapses.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We do not know how long COVID-19 will last.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are entering a new situation, a new normal, where enhanced personal hygiene habits and social responsibility will have to be an integral part of our lives.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Let us work together to make SG Clean our new way of life.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: SG Clean and our fight against dengue go hand-in-hand, as we remove stagnant water and keep our environment clean and litter-free.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This year, the Aedes mosquito population remains high, and indeed we are concerned about the increasing number of cases of the less common dengue virus serotype 3, or DENV-3.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We must be careful as Singapore has not seen a DENV-3 outbreak in almost three decades, and population immunity to DENV-3 is low.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, NEA conducts comprehensive surveillance of the mosquito population via more than 64,000 Gravitraps nation-wide.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This allows NEA to target its operations early and prioritise areas with higher mosquito population.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Second, NEA leverages technology, such as using drones to aid inspections or apply insecticide in hard-to-reach places.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Third, NEA shares data on dengue clusters and areas with higher mosquito population publicly on its website and myENV App.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This facilitates early community intervention and pre-emptive measures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I strongly urge all Singaporeans, young and old, to take proactive measures to protect yourselves and your loved ones.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Actively practise the "7 Habits of Good Public Hygiene" and "Mozzie Wipe-out".

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We can all show our support for the cleaners by playing our part too.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: At hawker centres for instance, we can do so by eating from our trays and returning them, as Mr Alex Yam has rightly pointed out.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have achieved a tray return rate of 62% on average at our Productive Hawker Centres, double that of other hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This was achieved through a	suite of efforts such as implementing salient reminders, providing strategically-located Automated Tray Return Stations, and ensuring that trays are clean and dry for use.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue working with stakeholders to promote tray return at all our hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This will also alleviate the cleaners’ workload so	that they can focus their efforts on maintaining general cleanliness.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As custodians of our much loved hawker culture, we will continue to work closely with stakeholders to ensure that affordable and good hawker food can continue to be a mainstay in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Mr Amrin Amin, Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap spoke about new hawker centres and the SEHCs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ten more are currently in the design or construction stage, and we are working out details for the remaining three.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA will tender out these two centres to socially-conscious enterprise.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These operators provide active management to build up clientele and vibrancy at hawker centres, such as through curating food mix and programming.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Currently, there are seven hawker centres under the Socially-Conscious Enterprise Hawker Centre, or SEHC, model, and most have done well.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Nonetheless, we will constantly review and improve the model.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When evaluating tender proposals for operating future hawker centres, NEA will give greater emphasis to footfall, vibrancy, and sustaining the hawker trade.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will also assess operators' performance in maintaining high footfall and stall occupancy.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In the past year, NEA introduced the Staggered Rent Scheme, and extended the Productive Hawker Centre grant to stallholders at SEHCs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA also reviewed the contracts between operators and stallholders to better safeguard stallholders' welfare, and required operators to conduct regular Hawkers’ Feedback Groups.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap's	question about stallholders’	feedback, these are usually on what more operators can do to improve vibrancy, attract footfall and help stallholders with their operations.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: All in, these measures serve to ensure that the SEHC model continues to benefit residents, and support stallholders at the same time.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I assure our hawkers that we will always look out for them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This will help them	with their	operating costs	during the current COVID-19 situation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: About one third of the stallholders, whose monthly rentals are below $200, will in fact enjoy more than one month of rental waiver.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We share Ms Joan Pereira's concern – we will monitor the situation and are prepared to provide further assistance if required.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Nonetheless, I am heartened to see the resilience of our stallholders.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: At Chinatown Complex Market, the stallholders are working hard to achieve the SG Clean quality mark for their stalls, and are even organising a promotion event this weekend.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is okay to, you know, gain a few calories or inches.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Last year, we also facilitated the formation of two Workgroups, which Mr Liang Eng Hwa spoke about, to co-create solutions to key issues facing our hawker trade and culture.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I am pleased to note that even before the Workgroups submit their recommendations, we are already adopting some of their ideas.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, we have already implemented one of their ideas, the Hawkers' Development Programme (HDP).

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Classes start next month, and I encourage aspiring hawkers to apply.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Workgroup also suggested fostering a strong hawkers’ network and facilitating hawker-to-hawker sharing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Following the positive feedback for the inaugural Hawkers' Seminar held last year, we will support the Federation of Merchants’ Associations, Singapore to organise this Hawkers' Seminar as an annual event.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Another Workgroup idea that we are	working on is a series of hawker awards to recognise hawkers’ efforts and achievements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will share details on the awards and nomination process later.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: A key challenge that the Workgroup raised was the physically demanding nature of the hawker trade.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We had launched the Hawkers' Productivity Grant (HPG) in 2017 to help stallholders adopt kitchen automation equipment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: You might have tried the ayam penyet by Mr Abdul Rahman Bin Suradi.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: He tapped on the HPG to buy a multi-function food processor to prepare his chilli sauce.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Now he needs only a quarter of the time and can ensure the correct consistency and quality.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With the time saved, he can serve more customers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To help more hawkers improve their productivity, I am pleased to announce that we have taken in the Workgroup's suggestion to enhance the HPG.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will also extend the HPG, which would have ended in October this year, to March 2023.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: (In Mandarin):   Hawkers are the heart and soul of our hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To help our stallholders tide over the COVID-19 situation, we will provide one-month of rental waiver, with the minimum sum of $200, to all stallholders in our hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Stallholders will receive 50% rental waiver this month and 25% in April and May.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have also listened to feedback from hawkers and will be enhancing the Hawkers' Productivity Grant to help more hawkers adopt productivity solutions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: From the 9 March 2020, market stallholders will also be able to apply for the HPG, and a broader range of items will be supported, such as queue management systems.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will also extend the HPG to March 2023.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: (In English): Today, as is fast becoming customary of MEWR's COS, besides Minister's treat of a meatless satay and gyoza from Impossible Meat, I have arranged for some hawker delights to be served in the Members' Room.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I urge all of you to tuck into these drool-worthy eats, if you have not done so.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The kentang and sardine epok are from Kalsom Kuih Muih Curry Puff at Yishun Park Hawker Centre, lovingly handmade by Mdm Kalsom Kamis and Mr Zaidi Bin Zainal and are simply sedap!

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Also, try the exquisite cakes from The Headless Baker at Ghim Moh Hawker Centre – you might just fall head over heels for them!

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is a new Incubation Stall run by Ms Amber Pong, who used to work as a pastry chef in Melbourne.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Building a sustainable and climate-resilient Singapore for ourselves and for future generations is not only about addressing our challenges.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Mr Mohamed Irshad and Mr Desmond Choo pointed out, it also brings economic opportunities for our companies and creates good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Local companies can leverage sustainability as a competitive advantage to export their innovative solutions and grow beyond our shores.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: An example is Orinno Technology Pte Ltd, one of NEA’s key partners in Project Wolbachia.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA and Orinno have jointly developed innovative Wolbachia-Aedes solutions, and have even filed five patents!

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Not only has Orinno played an important role in advancing Singapore’s public health research, they have also gone on to export these solutions, such as to Thailand and Australia.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Through upskilling and technology adoption, more than 45,000 people will benefit from higher value jobs in the environmental services, water and agri-food sectors over the next five to 10 years.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: He believes in constantly upskilling oneself and has completed over 20 courses from	cleaning, work-at-height, productivity management, risk management, Leadership & People Management courses, and the list goes on!

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Through his training, Mr Soh has been promoted to become an Operations Manager and now has more than a hundred people under his supervision.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As we move towards a risk-calibrated co-regulation approach,	we	will	support	companies	and	entire industries to build up their competencies and create higher value jobs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Just as how the Water Efficiency Management Plan created Water Efficiency Manager roles in companies, strengthening our environmental sanitation and food hygiene will also create demand for higher-skilled roles, such as the cross-functional Environmental Control Officers or ECOs, and Food Hygiene Officers (FHOs).

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA will be enhancing the competencies of ECOs who are currently engaged at construction sites as advisers of good environmental practices.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We	will	further	review	the	ECO	scheme	as	a competency-based vocation and broaden their	work areas beyond construction sites to more premises types, like shopping malls.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In time, ECOs will be valued as certified experts who are well-versed in multiple aspects of environmental management.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They are leaders who can drive and raise environmental standards of the premises	they	oversee.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In some	ways,	ECOs	are almost as important as CEOs!

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As part of SFA’s regular review of the Food Hygiene Officer course curriculum, SFA will enhance the training framework for FHOs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: FHOs can look forward to a holistic food safety education to better equip them as food safety guardians at their workplaces.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: SFA will also be developing a new Advanced FHO framework, which would allow FHOs to upgrade and progress to Advanced FHOs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Advanced FHOs will be trained to develop and implement internationally recognised Food Safety Management Systems.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Courses under these training frameworks can also be offered as certifiable modules to students in food-related programmes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This enhances their relevant skills and increase their job opportunities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There will also be exciting jobs created in new growth areas such as the high-tech agri-food sector.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: SFA has been working with government agencies, Institutes of Higher Learning and the industry to build competency within the agri-food workforce.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This includes developing training programmes at various levels, which will be rolled out at the right time to meet industry needs without creating oversupply.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In the last two years, SFA has collaborated with Temasek and Republic Polytechnics to implement two SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programmes leading to diplomas in Aquaculture and Urban Agricultural Technology respectively.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These programmes equip fresh ITE graduates with relevant skillsets to start their careers as Aqua or Agri Technicians.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Thus far, there are seven ITE graduates in the two Earn and Learn programmes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As an Aquaculture Technician at Apollo Aquaculture, Germaine benefited from	structured on-the-job training, mentorship and technical training.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This programme will cover contemporary topics on urban agri-technology, such as post-harvest of agriculture produce and novel food such as microalgae and insects.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I believe technology will remove the "yuck" factor and bring the "yum" factor in.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The scholarship provides scholars with financial support during their studies and attractive salary and clear progression pathways upon graduation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In tandem with the implementation of the Zero Waste Masterplan and Resource Sustainability Act, industry transformation will create more career opportunities requiring engineering, science and environmental management expertise.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I therefore want to assure aspiring entrants into these fields that the jobs are exciting, pay well, leverage on new technology, and most importantly, are Planet-saving!

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Chairman, I want to end off my speech on an optimistic note.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Even as the existential challenge of climate change looms over us, opportunities abound.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have to seize them and find creative solutions to make the most out of them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ms Chuan told me that 56 million kg of plastic had been used to make cassette tapes since they were first introduced in 1963.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I am not sure how many Members here remember or know what a cassette tape looks like.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: She gives them a new lease of life by upcycling discarded cassette tapes, weaving them into the "fabric" for new products such as this evening bag, and also this prototype houndstooth matching blouse.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I do not have much to show except this shirt which I have worn for five years.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And that is the best to go towards zero waste.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, to tackle this emergency, can we look into reducing the time frame, which means can we at least look into increasing it by 2025, which is five years' time instead of 10 years?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I am just wondering whether MEWR has done any studies or review into the studies that show that there is a positive effect of public disclosure.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, what is holding us back from doing something that will help to reduce emissions here in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The carbon tax is only one of many measures that we have put in to make sure that we nudge our industry, our transport, our buildings towards meeting our targets.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But there is also a reason behind that, like I mentioned in the early part of my speech.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is to make sure that we too will do our part in the United Nations' framework for climate change.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, even if we were to halve or eliminate our total GHG, we would not have moved the needle.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is all these other big emitters that must do their part to make sure that we can save our planet.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is important that in the context of which we look at commitments, it is also to look at the constraints and the context of each country's make-up of how they produce these GHG in the first place.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There was a second question on public disclosure.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I do not know how we can draw clear causality between the rules around disclosure and the outcomes around reducing GHG.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Surely, there are many other things that have nudged or transform these companies to achieve reduction in the GHG emissions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I am quite sure one of them is the UNFCCC framework itself because it has set a mood in the whole world, that countries, companies, had better moved, had better transformed, whether or not you are going to be transparent or otherwise, because that is where the world is going.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And out of responsibility or even out of marketability of the products, that is how people will move.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Chairman, I have a clarification concerning Project Wolbachia, the mosquito study.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The first is that, I think it has gone through a few phases now.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And from what I understand to date, it has not been deployed in any dengue clusters.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: My clarification first is, is there any rationale for not deploying it in dengue clusters thus far?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The second clarification is, earlier Minister Masagos mentioned that there is an intention to expand the project to larger areas.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Does he foresee, for example, in the coming months that this will also involve dengue clusters in the expanded project?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are extremely careful in deploying this technology because we are introducing something that is, while natural – Wolbachia is naturally occurring in mosquitoes – we are doing it artificially.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are injecting huge numbers into the community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, apart from the effectiveness of the technology, we are also mindful, as Mr Louis Ng had mentioned, of the disamenities that residents may suffer from suddenly having millions and millions of mosquitoes in their neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, there is some socialisation that has to take place.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But the disamenities and the complaints have persisted.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When I do my house visits, residents will still say they see a lot of mosquitoes now.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Then, when I explain to them it is the Project Wolbachia.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: What shall do?" I tell them, "Do whatever you need to do – spray, hit – do whatever you need to do to make sure you do not suffer from these dis-amenities".

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I think we need time to make sure that as we expand the areas where we deploy the Wolbachia, that the people are also used to this.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We hope that, as we suppress the mosquito population, we can then introduce fewer male mosquitoes over time.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But that is still a hope; that is still something we need to try and we need to validate.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Project Wolbachia will take some time but it is going to be a very important tool that we can use in times when climate change brings higher temperatures, which in turn, encourages mosquito breeding.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We need to have an arsenal of weapons to deploy.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the meantime, we must still do what we must do, which is to suppress the breeding of these mosquitoes within our homes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Project Wolbachia will not be a magic bullet.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We still need to ensure the breeding in our homes is well controlled.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: For Project Wolbachia, I was one of the first few constituencies.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, if you want to bring it back, I volunteer my constituency again.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: My clarification for the Minister revolves around food resilience.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: As I mentioned earlier, our plan to have 30% of our food supplies coming from within local produce by 2030 is an ambitious plan.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But as I said, if there is a way to bring this to achieve it earlier, I think we should really go all out to to do it.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But we also know that local produce inevitably comes at a higher cost and therefore, we should also think of ways to help local producers to be better accepted by the consumers here.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Many of my business associates in this industry, we want them to succeed but I think we need to do a lot more to get the consumers to accept it.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And I am sure Government can think of other ways to promote their products and for consumers to lend their support, not just by words, but by action.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If you are all familiar with the four Ps of marketing, it is not just about pricing.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Pricing is just one point at which we can push products faster.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Sometimes, pricing, if it is too cheap, like salt becomes a useless product.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And therefore, we will be helping our local producers to learn how to market their product better.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, Red Mart is now marketing the local produce, selling through the electronic means, through Internet.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is achieving some measure of success because they know how to market it properly.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is not just about shelf display and so forth.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Apart from that, we also have achieved some form of scale.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is particularly important for our fish industry.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The technologies we have put into our fish industry are quite costly.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And if they only do it in Singapore, they will not be able to achieve the scale per unit.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, we are happy that they have now expanded beyond Singapore shores.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, Apollo has got concessions now in Brunei, Barramundi Asia too, as well as some other of our fish farms.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And this will enable them to achieve and spread the cost of their early investments over a larger unit, a larger production.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: That too will help us to achieve the pricing points that would be attractive to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But beyond that, I think there is also a segment of our buyers who are looking for sustainable products.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The number may not be big but over time, the young will demand that products that they buy are sustainable ones.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, it is important for our local producers to learn how to produce these sustainably.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: On that note, I acknowledge the points made by Senior Minister of State on studies done and workgroups to be formed to look into that prospect.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My question relates to point I made in the Budget debate speech about waste in general and the amount of waste that we dispose.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I understand last year, MEWR had a target to reduce the amount of waste that is sent to Pulau Semakau by 30%.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: How is that coming along, by 2030, I believe was the timeline?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: On that note, what is the Minister's assessment of Pulau Semakau as a continued area where we dispose our waste?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: One of the these would be on the three key waste streams – e-waste, packaging waste and food waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That will help to reduce the amount of waste, including those that may be trashed to Semakau.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If we implement the Deposit Return Scheme, post-consumer plastics, like PET bottles and so on, will then not have to be trashed if we can create a demand for this as feedstock.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Then, other ideas, which I have mentioned in my speech, about chemical recycling – again to recycle the contaminated plastics, turn them into "NEWOil", for instance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: All these measures will help us to reduce the amount of waste that will go to Semakau landfill.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We want to extend the lifespan of Semakau landfill for as long as possible.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Road pavements – we are going to do a study later on, on its effectiveness and impact.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If you can use incineration bottom ash, that means instead of filling it up, putting in Semakau landfill, if you can actually use incineration bottom ash as construction material, NEWSand, then you will also reduce the amount of waste that you have to landfill in Semakau.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: My question is on solar installation at the reservoirs.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: I was wondering about the recovery of the capital expenditure or capex, compared with so-called the conventional energy.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: Of course, I am in support of this project to use solar energy, but I just want to understand whether, in the long run, is it something worthwhile to do.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I just came back from Saudi and they are deploying solar panel fields – these are so huge and I am so envious that they have so much land.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, not only do they have energy under the ground, they now have energy above the ground.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They have so much energy that they are not using it at all most of the time.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They just want to do it because there is the land that they have and they think this is the way to go to be green.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I can hear all the delicious food calling us.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, would Er Dr Lee Bee Wah do us a favour and withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I am very happy to hear of all the job opportunities.

text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.12 pm until 4.30 pm.
